description: Number of datasets. ndtset=0 means single-dataset mode (equivalent to 1). In multi-dataset runs, append a numeric suffix to variable names (e.g., ecut1, ecut2) to distinguish parameters across datasets.
name: ndtset

description: Plane-wave basis kinetic energy cutoff in Hartree. Larger values improve accuracy at higher computational cost. Typical values: NC pseudopotentials 20-40 Ha, PAW pseudopotentials 8-20 Ha (used together with pawecutdg).
name: ecut

description: Double-grid cutoff energy for PAW calculations in Hartree. Typically 2-4 times ecut. Required only for PAW pseudopotential calculations.
name: pawecutdg

description: Exchange-correlation functional selector. Common values: 1=LDA(Teter-Pade), 7=LDA(PW), 11=PBE(GGA), 24=HSE06, -116133=PBE0. Negative values select the corresponding LibXC functional by its ID.
name: ixc

description: Scaling factors for the primitive lattice vectors, consisting of 3 values in Bohr (default). Combined with rprim to define the lattice: actual lattice vector = acell[i] * rprim[i]. A unit label may be appended, e.g., acell 10.26 10.26 10.26 Bohr or acell 5.431 5.431 5.431 Angstrom.
name: acell

description: Primitive lattice vectors (dimensionless), one vector per row, 3 rows total. Combined with acell to obtain lattice vectors in Bohr. Example for an FCC primitive cell: 0 0.5 0.5 / 0.5 0 0.5 / 0.5 0.5 0.
name: rprim

description: Total number of atoms in the unit cell. Must match the number of rows in xred or xcart and the length of the typat array.
name: natom

description: Number of atom types. Must equal the length of the znucl array; the maximum value in typat must not exceed ntypat.
name: ntypat

description: Array of atom type indices (length = natom), 1-based. The maximum value must not exceed ntypat. Example: typat 1 1 means both atoms belong to the first atom type.
name: typat

description: Atomic number (nuclear charge) for each atom type; array length = ntypat. Examples: Si=14, C=6, O=8, Fe=26.
name: znucl

description: Reduced (fractional) atomic coordinates, 3 values per row, natom rows total. Coordinates are relative to the lattice vectors, typically in [0, 1).
name: xred

description: Cartesian atomic coordinates in Bohr, 3 values per row, natom rows total. Mutually exclusive with xred; only one of the two may be set.
name: xcart

description: k-point generation scheme. 1=automatic (Monkhorst-Pack with symmetry); 2=automatic (without time-reversal symmetry); 3=manual (requires nkpt and kpt); 0=no k-points (molecular calculation).
name: kptopt

description: Monkhorst-Pack k-point grid dimensions, 3 integers (nkx nky nkz). Used together with shiftk. Larger grids improve accuracy but increase cost.
name: ngkpt

description: k-point grid shifts (fractional coordinates relative to ngkpt), 3 values. Common values: 0.5 0.5 0.5 (Gamma-centered offset); 0 0 0 (includes the Gamma point).
name: shiftk

description: Number of k-points specified manually. Used together with the kpt array when kptopt=3.
name: nkpt

description: Manually specified k-point list in fractional coordinates, 3 values per row, nkpt rows total. Used when kptopt=3.
name: kpt

description: Maximum number of SCF iterations. If SCF does not converge within nstep steps, ABINIT stops and reports a warning. Increasing nstep can help for difficult systems.
name: nstep

description: SCF convergence criterion: SCF is considered converged when the absolute difference in total energy between consecutive steps is less than toldfe (in Hartree). Mutually exclusive with tolvrs and tolwfr.
name: toldfe

description: SCF convergence criterion: SCF is converged when the variance of the potential residual falls below tolvrs. Mutually exclusive with toldfe and tolwfr. Recommended for PAW calculations.
name: tolvrs

description: SCF convergence criterion: SCF is converged when the wavefunction residual falls below tolwfr. Mutually exclusive with toldfe and tolvrs. Suitable for non-self-consistent (NSCF) or response-function calculations.
name: tolwfr

description: SCF iteration scheme. Common values: 2=simple mixing (Pulay); 5=energy prediction (CG); 7=Pulay mixing (recommended); 17=improved Pulay; -2=non-self-consistent (nscf).
name: iscf

description: Whether to write the wavefunction file (WFK). 0=do not write; 1=write (default). The WFK file is needed for subsequent NSCF or response-function calculations but can be large.
name: prtwf

description: Whether to write the charge density file (DEN). 0=do not write; 1=write (default). The DEN file is used for post-processing or restart calculations.
name: prtden

description: Output verbosity level. 0=standard; 1=more detailed; 2=very detailed. Increasing this value significantly enlarges the output file.
name: prtvol

description: Directory path containing pseudopotential files (quoted string). ABINIT searches this directory for the files listed in pseudos.
name: ppdirpath

description: Comma-separated list of pseudopotential filenames (quoted string). The number of filenames must equal ntypat. Example: pseudos "Si.psp8" or pseudos "Fe.psp8, O.psp8".
name: pseudos

description: Ionic motion algorithm. 0=fixed ions (SCF only); 2=BFGS quasi-Newton (relaxation, recommended); 3=Broyden method; 20=molecular dynamics (Verlet); 22=Langevin dynamics.
name: ionmov

description: Maximum number of ionic relaxation or MD steps. Must be set when ionmov != 0.
name: ntime

description: Cell optimization scheme. 0=fixed cell; 1=optimize volume (fixed shape); 2=fully optimize cell (shape and volume); 3=optimize c/a ratio; 4-9=constrain specific lattice vector components.
name: optcell

description: Maximum allowed cell volume expansion ratio relative to the initial cell during cell optimization. Used to pre-allocate memory. Setting it too small may cause calculation failure; too large wastes memory. Typical range: 1.05-1.15.
name: dilatmx

description: Smearing width applied to the plane-wave cutoff during cell optimization, in Hartree. Effective only when optcell != 0. Recommended value: 0.5 Ha, to avoid energy oscillations caused by discontinuities in the cutoff.
name: ecutsm

description: Number of MPI processes for band parallelism. The product npband * npfft * npkpt * nspinor * bandpp must equal the total number of MPI processes. Increasing npband makes better use of multi-core nodes.
name: npband

description: Number of MPI processes for FFT parallelism. npband * npfft * npkpt must equal the total number of MPI processes (or a factor thereof). Useful for systems with large FFT grids.
name: npfft

description: Number of MPI processes for k-point parallelism. npkpt must not exceed the total number of k-points. This is the most efficient parallelism strategy since k-points are independent.
name: npkpt
